info.title: Instafind API
info.description: The public API (`/api/public/v1`, no credential; the widget and shops call it, also on the search host https://s.instafind.io) and the integration API (`/api/integration/v1`, a site API key or an OAuth connection token). A path, a parameter or a field removed or changed here is a breaking change; a new one is not.

post.summary: Fill the Filters tab of an API-sourced index from candidates
post.description: Once the catalogue is in. The candidates come in the order the client wants them, with names in the shop's language; instafind leaves out those shoppers could not use (no value, one value nearly every product has, an attribute with a value per product) and fills the sidebar (8) and the search panel (4). Search behaviours are not changed. Does nothing once the Filters tab was saved (`already_set`). Ask again later after `no_products` (none searchable yet), `not_ready` (products still being made searchable, or written in the last minute) or `nothing_to_show` (no candidate worth showing; nothing is saved). At most 50 candidates. Needs the `indexes:manage` scope.

post.summary: Fill the Template tab of an API-sourced index with the client's templates
post.description: Once, when the client is set up. `results` is the product card of the full results page, `live_search` the row of the live search; each is widget template HTML with `{{field_id}}` placeholders and an optional `<style>` block, stored as a code-mode template the owner edits in the Template Builder. A view already set up there (a chosen layout or code) is left alone (`already_set`); a view not sent stays as it is (`not_sent`). Needs the `indexes:manage` scope.

parameters.description: Search-visibility policy. Omit (default) to return as soon as writes are durable; search reflects them within ~15s. `wait_for` blocks the response until the next refresh tick (≤15s) — use for read-after-write flows or on the final batch of a bulk import. `immediate` forces an ES refresh for sub-second visibility (more expensive — use sparingly).

post.description: Creates or updates up to 100 orders. The body must be JSON. Do not send customer details: `reference` must be a random value you generate and keep on the order, not the order number. To tell one customer's orders from another's, send `customer_key`: an HMAC-SHA256 in lowercase hex of something stable about the customer (such as the normalised email address), made with a secret that stays in the shop. instafind never gets the secret, so it cannot work out who the customer is. Left out, the stored key stays; null (or an empty string) removes it. A key erased through the DELETE customers route is dropped from every order placed before the erasure, whenever that order is sent again. Sending an order again replaces it, unless the stored version has a later `updated_at`, and then the order is reported as `stale`. One rejected order does not fail the others. A line has search credit when it carries both `search_query` and `search_index_id`; an unusable value, or an index outside this website, drops the credit and keeps the sale. Needs the `orders:write` scope on a key that covers all of the website's indexes.

parameters.name: website
parameters.description: UUID of the website

customer_key.description: HMAC-SHA256 of the customer, made with a secret only the shop has. Any other format rejects the order

lines.description: Not empty, unless `status` is `cancelled`. Empty, null or left out on a cancelled order, the lines already stored stay.

net_total.description: Line total without tax, after discounts

stale.description: A later version is already stored; nothing changed

results.description: In request order: {reference, status: ok|stale|error, reason?}

403.description: insufficient_scope (orders:write), or the key does not cover all indexes

404.description: not_found: no such website, or not the key's website

422.description: The request has no valid `orders` list

delete.description: Removes the `customer_key` from every order of this website that carries it, so those orders can no longer be told apart from anyone else's. The orders themselves stay in the revenue reports. instafind remembers the erasure for as long as it keeps orders, and drops the key from any order placed before it that is sent again; orders placed later keep it. Sending the same key again finds nothing and still answers 200. Needs the `orders:write` scope on a key that covers all of the website's indexes.

parameters.name: website
parameters.description: UUID of the website

parameters.name: customerKey
parameters.description: The `customer_key` the orders were sent with: 64 lowercase hex characters

forgotten_orders.description: How many orders carried the key

403.description: insufficient_scope (orders:write), or the key does not cover all indexes

404.description: not_found: no such website, not the key's website, or a customer key that is not 64 lowercase hex characters

post.description: Same request and response as `POST /api/v1/websites/{website}/search-indices`. Creates a search index with no feed behind it: the schema is supplied here and products are written through the Client Product Write API. The index is searchable immediately via /api/public/v1/search?id={id} and returns no results until products are written. Creation is all-or-nothing — on any failure nothing is left behind and the request can be retried.

parameters.name: website
parameters.description: Website UUID (slugs are only unique per organization, so /api/v1 binds websites by id)

langcode.description: Language driving the analyzers; must be a supported index strategy

backend_type.description: Optional; elasticsearch is the only supported backend

fields.description: The index schema. Exactly one field must have the type 'identifier' — it carries the product id used as the storage key, the document id and the delete key. Field types cannot be changed after creation.

field_id.description: Lowercase key the documents use for this field

type.description: FieldType value, e.g. title, price, identifier

403.description: Forbidden — the user cannot manage indices on this website

404.description: Website not found

409.description: index_deleted_during_creation — a delete of the new index arrived before it was finished; the delete wins and the index is purged. Send a new create request if the index is still needed

503.description: Either the durable product store is unavailable (`durable_storage_unavailable`), or creation failed and rolled back (`index_creation_failed`). Both leave nothing behind and carry Retry-After

get.description: Returns the popular searches of the specified search index, for the widget, ranked by how many distinct visitors (IP addresses) searched them; `count` is that number. Phrases the merchant hid are left out. Searches that found nothing are not served here: they show what a shop lacks and what shoppers typed, so they are read only on the authenticated analytics pages.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: UUID id of the search index

parameters.name: mode
parameters.description: The keyword mode. Only `popular` is served.

parameters.name: display_mode
parameters.description: The widget display mode asking (modal, dropdown-mega, dropdown-list), whose own popular-searches settings apply.

422.description: A required parameter is missing or invalid

get.description: Searches an index. The one text-search endpoint, for the widget's dropdown and results page and for API callers; the full contract is in docs/API_DOCUMENTATION.md.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The search index id.

parameters.name: context
parameters.description: Where the results are shown. dropdown: the widget's live views; promote rules shown in the dropdown apply, and no rule impressions are recorded. results: the results page, category pages and API callers.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: The search words. Without them, a request that filters, sorts or says browse=1 lists the matching products (browse); otherwise it is a health check.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of results to return. 0 returns the aggregations only, and is not recorded as a search.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: The page of `limit` results, from 1. Pages end at the 10,000th product.

parameters.name: facet_size
parameters.description: Values returned per facet. Selected values outside them are appended. facet_size[<field>]=<n> sets one facet's size, next to the scalar (or facet_size[*]) for the others: facet_size=10&facet_size[category_ids]=500. All facets share 5,000 values. A size that is not a positive number, or names a field that is not a facet, is reported in applied.ignored.

parameters.name: facets
parameters.description: Comma-separated field ids to aggregate; all facets when absent. A range field listed keeps its min/max.

parameters.name: facet_sort
parameters.description: count: most products first. key: A to Z (the first facet_size values by value, not the top values sorted).

parameters.name: category_matches
parameters.description: Up to this many (1-10) categories whose name matches the words, answered as `category_matches`: `[{value, label, highlight, path, subtitle, count}]` (`subtitle`: the subtitle of the category filter, null without one), best first (more of the words matched, then more products). The category field is set per index (Search settings → Categories); without one the list is empty. Not on a browse.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: A field switched Sortable, by its id or as sorted (`<field>.keyword` for text). Anything else keeps the relevance order and is reported in applied.ignored; `_score` asks for relevance order.

parameters.name: order
parameters.description: Required with sort.

parameters.name: browse
parameters.description: With 1 and no q, lists every product (with any filters, sort and paging), not a health check.

parameters.name: highlight
parameters.description: With 1, each hit whose title fields match the words carries `highlight.<field>`: the values with the match in <strong> tags. Off when the index turns highlighting off.

parameters.name: ignore_detected[]
parameters.description: A value from `detected` the shopper removed, as <field>:<value>: this search does not recognise it and searches its words like any others. Repeat for several.

parameters.name: strict
parameters.description: With 1, a search that would ignore any filter or its sort is refused with 422 filters_not_applied instead of answering without it. The response always reports what was applied under `applied`.

parameters.name: merchandising
parameters.description: With 2 (or higher), the client labels sponsored filter values and products, so sponsored rules may apply. Otherwise they are left out.

parameters.name: sid
parameters.description: The visitor's session id, for search analytics. Never a filter.

parameters.name: filters
parameters.description: Any other parameter is a filter on a field: `<field>[]=<value>` (repeat for several values), `<field>=<min>-<max>` on a range field. What could not be applied is reported in `applied.ignored`.

400.description: Missing id, or the search failed: `results.error`

404.description: No such index, or one that is not serving search: `index_not_found`

422.description: context is not dropdown or results (`invalid_context`), or strict=1 and some filters or the sort cannot be applied (`filters_not_applied`)

parameters.description: As on /api/public/v1/search.

parameters.description: With 1, refused (422 filters_not_applied) when a filter or the sort cannot be applied.

parameters.description: As on /api/public/v1/search: 2 when the client labels sponsored products.

parameters.name: sid

parameters.name: filters

get.summary: Products to suggest next to one or more products
get.description: The owner's picks first, then the products bought with them in the shop's orders, then (with fill=category) the best sellers of their category, as products in the /api/public/v1/search format and in that order; each hit has suggestion_source. 200.description: results, as on /api/public/v1/search; each hit has suggestion_source: manual, orders or category

400.description: Missing id, or the search failed

post.description: Form-encoded, so a browser beacon needs no preflight. Send one click per link to a product of the search response's `related` list, from the browser: a server-side call would count crawlers. Always 204, whatever it is sent.

get.description: Returns keyword suggestions based on popular search terms from the last 7 days in which a word starts with the input query, ignoring accents. Phrases that start with the input come first, then by how many distinct visitors (IP addresses) searched them. `occurrence` is that number. Spellings that differ only in accents count as one phrase. Phrases the merchant hid are not suggested.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: The partial search query to get suggestions for.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: UUID id of the search index

ContentSnippetPlacement.description: Where in the widget a snippet shows: before the visitor types, or when a search finds nothing (`{query}` in its text becomes the search text)

ContentSnippetPublicResource.description: Public content snippet for widget display

slug.description:
Minimal content snippet resource for public widget consumption.

Excludes internal fields (id, search_index_id, timestamps) to provide
only the data needed for widget rendering.

ErrorResponse.description: Generic API error response with a short error message and optional human-readable explanation.

error.description: Short error message or category. Most call sites use a sentence-form summary (e.g. "Missing id parameter", "Cannot delete feed: search indices still attached").
error.example: Cannot delete feed: search indices still attached

message.description: Human-readable explanation suitable for surfacing to API consumers.
message.example: Detach the indices listed under attached_indices before retrying.

rebuild_pending.description: The live index stores this field at another type: search, filters, sorting and value detection on it wait until the index is rebuilt

filtered.description: Stored, dropped by a preprocessor, removed from the index (API-sourced only)

pending.description: Stored durably, not yet searchable; a scheduled repair will finish it (API-sourced only). Do not re-send

reason.description: Why it was rejected (error) or is not yet searchable (pending)

results.description: The hits and facets; an empty array for a health check or when nothing was searched (see `reason`).

value.description: Every match, not just this page

_source.description: The fields marked "include in results", the product id among them

highlight.description: With highlight=1: per title field, the values with the match in <strong>

aggregations.description: `<field>_facet` terms buckets and `min_<field>` / `max_<field>` for range fields

redirect.description: The redirect rule this query names; the client navigates to `url`

query_used.description: What was searched instead of the words, when a correction ran; null otherwise

category_matches.description: With category_matches=<n>: categories named like the words, best first

applied.description: The filters the search used and those it ignored, with the reason

names.description: Names of the selected values, per field

SearchBehaviorCollection.description: The search behaviors of an index, one per field

sortable_fields.description: Fields whose type allows `sortable` (and, for a number field, once the live index maps it)

facetable_fields.description: Fields that allow `facet` (by type, and not waiting for a rebuild)

rangeable_fields.description: Fields that allow `range` (price and number fields, once the live index maps them)

searchable_fields.description: Fields that allow `searchable` (all but numbers and booleans, and not waiting for a rebuild)

rebuild_pending_fields.description: Fields whose type changed: search, filter, sort and value detection on them wait until the index is rebuilt (the next full sync of a feed index; the automatic rebuild of an API-sourced index)

latin_spelling_fields.description: Fields that allow `latin_spelling`. Null unless the index is Greek

rebuild_pending_behaviors.description: For each field in `rebuild_pending_fields`, the switches its new type allows once the index is rebuilt (searchable, fuzzy, facet, range, sortable, latin_spelling)

sort_label.description: The name in the sort dropdown. Empty uses the field id.

sortable.description: Searches may sort by it: the sort dropdown of the full results page and the search API `sort`

latin_spelling.description: A Greek query word also matches its Latin spellings in this field ("νικε" finds "Nike"). Read on Greek indexes only

value_detection.description: Recognising values of this field in queries. Null on fields whose values cannot be recognised (title, description, identifiers, numbers).

remove_words.description: A filter takes its words out of the text search. Off by default; ignored for a boost

SearchIndexResource.description: A search index and its field schema

id.description: Search index UUID; the value to pass as ?id= when searching

name.description: Resolved display name (user-supplied if set, otherwise 'Index <id>')

name_override.description: Raw user-supplied name; null when no override is set

source.description: Where products come from: imported from a feed, or written through the API

lifecycle_state.description: Whether the index accepts writes and configuration edits; an index is only writable while active

rebuild.description: The rebuild of an API-sourced index from its stored products, while one is running; null otherwise. Writes and search keep working during it; edits of fields, preprocessors and the price format answer 409 rebuild_in_progress until it is done

built.description: Products written into the new index so far

index_name.description: Physical Elasticsearch index backing this search index

StoredProduct.description: A product held in the durable store behind an API-sourced index, as the client sent it and as it was processed

product_uid.description: The product's identifier, exactly as the client supplied it

title.description: Display title, taken from the configured title field when the product was written

raw_data.description: The body the client sent, before any preprocessor ran. Null on a product that has no stored payload

processed_data.description: The document as it was indexed. Null when a preprocessor dropped the product — see `filtered`

filtered.description: True when a preprocessor dropped this product: it is stored, but deliberately not searchable

pending.description: True when the product's latest revision has not been confirmed by the search backend yet. It is stored durably and will become searchable; it is not lost

updated_at.description: When this product was last written

users_count.description: Number of direct members (when loaded; never returned to an API key)

search_indices_count.description: Number of search indices (when loaded; for an API key, only the indexes in its grant)

apiKey.description:
Sent as `Authorization: Bearer …`. Accepted by `/api/integration/v1` only. Two kinds of
credential reach it:

- a site API key (`ifk_…`), created by a site admin on the site's **API keys** page or with
  `php artisan api-keys:create`. It expires after at most a year and can be rotated with a
  grace period or revoked;
- an OAuth access token (`ifa_…`, valid for one hour) issued to an app connected through
  "Connect to instafind". The app renews it with its refresh token.

Either way the credential belongs to one website, not to a person. It holds scopes
(`indexes:read`, `indexes:manage`, `products:read`, `products:write`, `products:delete`,
`analytics:read`, `orders:write`) and covers either all of the site's indexes or a chosen list; anything
outside that answers 404, exactly like a missing record.

tags.name: Integration API
tags.description: /api/integration/v1 — the only endpoints a site API key reaches. Each needs one scope. The integration routes share controllers with the /api/v1 routes of the same path, so request and response bodies are documented there; errors use {error, message}: 401 invalid_api_key / api_key_revoked / api_key_expired, 403 insufficient_scope (with required_scope), 404 not_found (also for anything outside the key's website or index grant).
